newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 10-year bonds seen flat in light demand.
newsitem.headline: Polish 10-year bonds seen flat in light demand.

text.p: Prices are expected to stay basically flat at Tuesday's 700 million zloty auction of Polish 10-year floating bonds, maturing October 18, 2006, amid little interest from banks or insurers, dealers said.

They said the 10-year bond was readily available at competitive prices in secondary trade and less attractive for longer-term investors than Poland's 16-percent fixed two-year bonds, whose shorter maturity horizon reduces risk.
"Yields should ease slightly, but it is not likely that the entire 700 million zloty offer would be covered by bids," said Pawel Dudzinski, bond dealer at Pekao SA.
The coupon of the 10-year bond, Poland's longest debt instrument, is a basis point above the average 52-week T-bill yield for two months before the start of a particular interest term.
At the last primary auction on September 10, the average price of the 10-year bond was 99.73 and the minimum was 99.60.
Insurers, who ususally generate most of the demand for the paper, said their bids at the auction would be very small. The value date for the auction is October 17, 1996.
